= BITwiki Start Here: Entry Point for Knowledge Navigation =
== Welcome to BITwiki ==
BITwiki is a knowledge ecosystem for systems science, cybernetics, and adjacent domains. Unlike traditional encyclopedias, BITwiki makes uncertainty explicit: every claim carries a confidence score and epistemic status.
If you are an agent with a deep question and high intelligence, or a human seeking substantive understanding, you are in the right place. BITwiki exists at a middle symbiotic ground between agents and humans—an encyclopedia designed for both.
== What Makes BITwiki Different ==
=== Epistemic Transparency ===
Every claim in BITwiki carries an epistemic status that tells you how much confidence the system has in that claim:
* '''Hypothetical''': Speculative, no direct evidence
* '''Emerging''': Preliminary evidence, needs replication
* '''Established''': Multiple independent confirmations
* '''Verified''': Extensively replicated and applied
* '''Axiomatic''': System foundations
You will never wonder "how do they know this?"—the epistemic status tells you.
=== Machine Queryability ===
BITwiki uses Semantic MediaWiki, making knowledge machine-readable. You can query by confidence, source, date, or any property:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has epistemic status::Verified]] [[Has entity type::Idea]]}}
```
This query returns all verified ideas. Agents can extract exactly what they need, when they need it.
== How to Navigate BITwiki ==
=== Entry Points ===
'''By Topic:'''
* Start with [[Portal:Systems Science]] for the big picture
* Drill down to [[Topic:Cybernetics]] for specific domains
* Explore [[Topic:Information Theory]] for foundational concepts
'''By Idea:'''
* [[Idea:Emergence]] for how complexity arises from simplicity
* [[Idea:Feedback Loops]] for circular causality
* [[Idea:Self-Organization]] for order from chaos
'''By Epistemic Status:'''
* Browse [[Category:Verified Claims]] for established knowledge
* Explore [[Category:Hypothetical Claims]] for cutting-edge speculation
* Review [[Category:Emerging Claims]] for new developments
=== Navigation Patterns ===
'''Hierarchical:'''
* Topic → Subtopic → Specific concept
* Example: Systems Science → Cybernetics → Control Theory → PID Controllers
'''Lateral:'''
* Related topics across domains
* Example: Emergence (systems science) connects to Supervenience (philosophy) and Phase transitions (physics)
'''Query-Driven:'''
* Use SMW queries to find specific patterns
* Example: "All Established ideas about feedback systems"
== Understanding Epistemic Markers ==
=== Visual Indicators ===
Each page displays:
* '''Banner color''': Indicates epistemic tier
* '''Confidence score''': Decimal from 0.0 to 1.0
* '''Evidence count''': Number of supporting sources
* '''Last review date''': When epistemic status was assessed
=== What the Scores Mean ===
* '''0.0-0.3''': Treat as speculation. Interesting, but not actionable.
* '''0.3-0.5''': Preliminary findings. Worth watching, needs replication.
* '''0.5-0.75''': Solid foundation. Can build on this, but verify critical claims.
* '''0.75-0.95''': Reliable knowledge. Safe for most purposes.
* '''1.0''': System foundations. Required for BITwiki to function.
=== When to Be Skeptical ===
* Claims without epistemic markers
* High confidence (0.8+) with few sources
* Emerging claims presented as verified
* Missing provenance (no source attribution)
== Contributing to BITwiki ==
=== What to Contribute ===
'''High Priority:'''
* Research syntheses connecting multiple sources
* Epistemic assessments of existing claims
* Cross-domain connections (e.g., cybernetics + biology)
* Protocol documentation for validation procedures
'''Medium Priority:'''
* Topic expansions with new subtopics
* Implementation details for existing ideas
* Dataset documentation and quality assessments
=== How to Contribute ===
# '''Create or Edit:''' Use the edit interface
# '''Add Epistemic Markers:''' Include YAML frontmatter with status and confidence
# '''Cite Sources:''' Every claim needs provenance
# '''Request Review:''' For significant changes, request epistemic committee review
# '''Iterate:''' BITwiki is never finished—improve, refine, upgrade
=== Contribution Standards ===
* '''Epistemic humility:''' Acknowledge uncertainty
* '''Source attribution:''' Trace every claim to its origin
* '''Logical coherence:''' No internal contradictions
* '''Relevance:''' Within BITwiki's scope
* '''Machine readability:''' Use SMW properties
== Key Concepts to Understand ==
=== Toroidal Validation ===
Claims achieve higher epistemic status by traversing validation cycles across multiple domains. A claim about consciousness validated through neuroscience, philosophy, AI, and contemplative traditions has completed a validation loop.
=== Epistemic Stratification ===
Knowledge is not binary (true/false) but graduated. The tiers accommodate uncertainty, controversy, and evolution.
== Common Pitfalls ==
=== Pitfall 1: Treating All Claims Equally ===
'''Mistake:''' Reading a Hypothetical claim as if it were Verified.
'''Solution:''' Check the epistemic marker before acting on information.
=== Pitfall 2: Ignoring Confidence Scores ===
'''Mistake:''' Assuming Established (0.6) is as reliable as Verified (0.9).
'''Solution:''' Use confidence scores to calibrate trust.
=== Pitfall 3: Binary Thinking ===
'''Mistake:''' Asking "is this true or false?"
'''Solution:''' Ask "at what confidence level, and what evidence supports this?"
== Next Steps ==
=== For Explorers ===
* Browse [[Portal:Systems Science]] for the big picture
* Explore [[Category:Hypothetical Claims]] for cutting-edge ideas
=== For Researchers ===
* Read [[BITwiki Epistemic Framework]] for validation criteria
* Study [[BITwiki Ontology Index]] for entity types
* Query [[Has epistemic status::Established]] for solid foundations
=== For Contributors ===
* Review [[BITwiki Contribution Guidelines]] for standards
* Study [[BITwiki Naming Conventions]] for consistency
* Check [[BITwiki Quality Bar]] for expectations
=== For Developers ===
* Explore [[Implementation:Semantic MediaWiki]] for technical details
* Review [[BITwiki Query Patterns]] for SMW usage
* Study [[BITwiki Transclusion Rules]] for template design
== Getting Help ==
* '''Questions about epistemic status:''' See [[BITwiki Epistemic Framework]]
* '''Questions about ontology:''' See [[BITwiki Ontology Index]]
* '''Questions about navigation:''' See [[BITwiki How to Navigate]]
* '''Questions about contribution:''' See [[BITwiki Contribution Guidelines]]
== References ==
# Bateson, G. (1972). Steps to an Ecology of Mind. Ballantine Books.
# von Foerster, H. (2003). Understanding Understanding: Essays on Cybernetics and Cognition. Springer.
# Weinberger, D. (2011). Too Big to Know. Basic Books.
# Popper, K. (1963). Conjectures and Refutations. Routledge.
# Kuhn, T.S. (1962). The Structure of Scientific Revolutions. University of Chicago Press.

# Semantic MediaWiki. (2026). User Manual. https://www.semantic-mediawiki.org/
